:::{.gray-text .center-text}
*Cleaning and organising data takes 60% of a data scientist's time. Survey of data scientists, CrowdFlower, 2016.*
:::

Yesterday we interrogated a table that behaved itself. Today we will meet one that does not, and
will spend the whole day learning how to wrangle it into something useful.

Day 4 has three new code patterns, and we meet them in the order the day runs. This morning
we'll learn a **missing-data pattern** that decides what to do about gaps, and then we get
formally introduced to functions, after seeing their utility during yesterday's EOD activity.
This afternoon's first session covers the two remaining patterns together: first the
**derived-column pattern** that adds a new column to hold your answer (because what you actually
need is almost never what is contained in the raw data!), and then the **string-cleaning
pattern** that tidies up messy text so that comparisons can work.
